messages:
maya: Heads up — customer reported p99 latency spike after we flipped their canary to int8 with KV cache enabled on model redwood/opt-6.7b-int8. p50 looks fine, but p99 ~2.5x baseline. Any KV cache/quant interactions we should know about? :eyes:

sam: can you paste the customer id and a sample request id? also is this across regions or single region?

maya: cust: acme-widget (acct-742), example req id: rq_0a1b2c3d. Region us-west2 only for now.

ryan: we saw similar behavior once where prefix-KV cache warmed oddly with int8 kernels — cache hits returned slightly larger internal tensors causing extra memcpy in runtime path. usually a small bump but can amplify at p99 when batches are tiny.

jordan: do we have repro script? can we toggle kv_cache and repro?

maya: repro steps I used:
```
# minimal repro
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY"
  -d '{"model":"redwood/opt-6.7b-int8","input":"summarize: ...","client_request_id":"rq_0a1b2c3d"}'
```
I also ran 1000 parallel single-shot requests (concurrency 8) and captured tail latencies.

lee: handy to capture node-level traces: heap/alloc, memcpy stats, and kernel time. ops-bot can dump a perf slice.

ops-bot: scheduled perf capture on node gpu-12 for 90s, collecting nvprof, runtime logs, and KV cache metrics. link: https://perf.redwood.internal/slices/3367890123

sam: short-term mitigation for that customer: set model override to fp16 or disable KV cache on their route. Which is less disruptive?

maya: customer already prefers int8 for cost. They asked if we can avoid rollback. If disabling KV cache buys time maybe that is acceptable.

ryan: disabling KV cache should remove the memcpy edge case. alternative: switch their canary traffic to int8+no-kvcache or to fp16 with KV cache on. FP16 will increase cost ~1.9x.

jordan: can we push a config-level fallback so that if p99 exceeds threshold we auto-fallback to fp16 for that route?

lee: we have a per-route override API. Example config:
```
{"route":"/v1/models/redwood/opt-6.7b-int8","overrides":{"quant_profile":"fp16","kv_cache":false}}
```
I can apply to acct-742 for immediate mitigation.

maya: please apply KV cache=false on acct-742 canary and monitor for 30m.

jordan: logged incident and assigned to eng-runtime (INC-2023-742). Also adding eng-ml to thread for quant validation.

ryan: long-term, we should: 1) add unit tests that combine quant profiles + KV cache with small batch scenarios, 2) add metric in console that correlates KV cache hit rate with memcpy/host-transfer time, 3) consider kernel path optimization to avoid extra copies when cache shapes mismatch.

sam: action items:
- lee: apply override (kv_cache=false) now and confirm rollback plan (5m)
- maya: collect 1h tail logs and sample payloads
- ryan: review kernel memcpy hotspots and propose fix by EOW
- jordan: keep customer notified, offer temporary credits if perf hit persists

lee: applied override to acct-742 canary at 3367890155. New route config posted.

ops-bot: metric alert cleared for p99 on acct-742 at 3367890178 (p99 down to baseline * 1.05).

maya: confirming — p99 looks back to normal on their canary, customer notified. Thanks team. :tada:

support-bot: reminder — please attach logs and perf slice to INC-2023-742 ticket before closing.

jordan: keeping ticket open until ryan's kernel fix lands or until we have a validated regression test.

maya: adding suggested test vectors and small-batch harness to the ticket now.

ryan: will prototype a zero-copy path for the mismatched-kv case; target PR in 3 working days.

maya: great — will follow up after PR and postmortem.
